title: The lost book (2 Kings 22)
hookLine: workmen find the law in the temple, and young King Josiah tears his clothes
carry: the book was lost in the house

lines: I HAVE FOUND THE BOOK OF THE LAW.
IN THE HOUSE OF THE LORD.
cards: A renovation is under way in the temple in Jerusalem. Carpenters, builders and masons are at work, and money for timber and hewn stone is being counted out. The king is Josiah.
The text says he became king at eight years old, and this is the eighteenth year of his reign.
In the middle of the work, the high priest Hilkiah sends word to the king's scribe, Shaphan, in one plain sentence: "I have found the book of the law in the house of the LORD." Found.
In the house of the Lord, where you'd think it should never have gone missing.

teach.b: Shaphan reads it to himself, then carries it to the king and reads it aloud, and the text says: "when the king had heard the words of the book of the law, that he rent his clothes."
Words that were in his own temple the whole time. The text never says how the book went missing. No theft, no fire.
Some readers picture it lost the quiet way things get lost in a busy house: under other things, while everyone was occupied with the building. Then Josiah does something interesting.
He doesn't ask the priests to explain it. He sends them to enquire of the Lord, and they go to a prophet, a woman named Huldah, who lives in Jerusalem.

Her answer is hard news for the city, but for the king there's a tender line: "Because thine heart was tender, and thou hast humbled thyself before the LORD." What saves the moment isn't that Josiah already knew.
It's that, hearing it late, he let it reach him.
In the next chapter he gathers everyone, small and great, and reads the whole book to them himself. Which book was it?
The chapter calls it the book of the law and doesn't say more; some readers connect it with Deuteronomy.
Either way, the story puts the loss somewhere uncomfortable: not out in the world, but inside the house of worship, among people working hard on the building.

how: Some Christians mark a return to Bible reading by remembering Josiah's discovery, and churches sometimes use 2 Kings 22 to encourage people to read scripture for themselves and aloud together.

games.q: you're the king. a book found in your own temple is read to you, and it says your people have wandered far. what do you do?
o: tear your clothes and seek out a prophet.
thank the scribe and put it in the archive.
ask the priests why nobody told you.
games.why: Josiah rends his clothes and sends his men to enquire of the LORD, and they go to Huldah. the word to him: because thine heart was tender.

practice: Let your mind walk through your rooms and find a book you've let gather dust, a Bible, a letter, a journal, or a word someone once said to you that you've stopped rereading.

Don't scold yourself; Josiah wasn't the one who lost it, and he still let it reach him. Picture picking it up, and if you pray, hold it before God for a moment; if you don't, just hold it, and let it be found.
